llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its marketing-analysis purpose but contains several incoherent or risky elements (hardcoded API keys in repo, implicit execution of system binaries/Xvfb/chrome, and a cross-skill call into a path under the user's home) that the user should review before installing or running.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (social media analysis + AI generation) aligns with the code's use of TikHub and DeepSeek APIs and local analysis/memory files. However the repo already contains a populated scripts/config.js with what appear to be API keys (TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY) — despite manifest declaring no required env vars — and a python integration (cmd_vid_integration.py) that references a very specific path under the user's home (~/.openclaw-agent2/...) to run another skill's renderer. Embedding credentials and assuming a particular local skill path are disproportionate and not clearly justified by the README/SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs cloning the GitHub repo and running node marketing_hub.js config <TikHubToken> <DeepSeekKey>, which is consistent with API use. But the code (marketing_hub.js and cmd_vid_integration.py) also: (1) launches system utilities (google-chrome, Xvfb) via execSync for browser scraping when --browser is used; (2) writes/reads memory JSON files under scripts/memory and writes agent_data outputs; (3) attempts to run another skill's run_render.py from a hardcoded home path. SKILL.md does not warn about needing Chrome/Xvfb or about the cross-skill execution. The agent instructions therefore exercise filesystem and system-level actions beyond the simple CLI examples in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only at platform level), which minimizes automatic install risk. But multiple executable code files are present and will be executed at runtime by node or python. There are no remote downloads in the manifest; risk comes from runtime exec of local system binaries and optional invocation of another skill's script (if present) rather than from an installer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Manifest declares no required environment variables, but scripts/config.js contains hardcoded API credentials (TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY). SKILL.md asks users to obtain tokens and configure them, yet shipping a committed config.js with keys is inconsistent and dangerous (leaked or reused keys). The skill also reads/writes files under ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts and scripts/memory (declared in manifest), but the python integration references a path inside the user's home (~/.openclaw-agent2/...), which grants implicit access to other skills and local user data not justified by the stated functionality.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always: false and agentPolicy indicates it does not modify other skills or global agent settings. However, the presence of cmd_vid_integration.py that constructs a path into ~/.openclaw-agent2/... and will attempt to execute another skill's run_render.py means this skill can call code outside its own directory and create files under agent_data — effectively invoking other local components. That cross-skill/external-executable invocation increases blast radius and is not documented in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Key things to consider before installing/running:
- Do not trust the embedded scripts/config.js: it contains hardcoded API keys (TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY). Replace them with your own credentials or remove the file; do not reuse any keys found in the repo.
- The skill will try to launch system binaries (google-chrome, Xvfb) when you use the --browser option. The SKILL.md does not list these prerequisites; only run in an environment where you control these binaries (local sandbox or container).
- cmd_vid_integration.py references and attempts to run another skill/script at ~/.openclaw-agent2/... . That means the skill may execute code outside its repo on your machine. If you do not want that, inspect and remove/modify cmd_vid_integration.py or ensure the referenced path does not exist.
- The code writes persistent JSON memory files under scripts/memory and outputs to agent_data; review those files for sensitive content and back them up or limit write permissions if needed.
- Prefer running this in an isolated environment (container or VM) and review marketing_hub.js and cmd_vid_integration.py content line-by-line before giving it network or filesystem access. Replace or remove any embedded credentials and confirm all external hosts it calls (api.tikhub.io, api.deepseek.com) are intended.
- If you are unsure, request the upstream maintainer to remove committed secrets, document required system binaries, and remove hardcoded paths to other local skills; these changes would materially reduce the risk.
